card.name: Inside drug and enzyme names
card.fires_on: Words in the middle of a drug or enzyme name or a short linking word, in label text on lipid drugs and vitamin D analogs. Examples are the P in Cytochrome P450, the first letter of lomitapide, and the R in RAYALDEE.

modes.label: Start of a drug name
modes.description: The first letter or two of a drug name that is split into pieces, such as lomitapide or RAYALDEE.
modes.example: Other lipid modifying agents:<< l>>omitapide ↑ lovastatin ↑

modes.label: Enzyme name or linking word
modes.description: A letter in Cytochrome P450, or a small word like of or to just before a drug name.
modes.example: Moderate or Strong Cytochrome<< P>>450 3A4 In

modes.label: List comma
modes.description: A comma inside a list of drug names.

card.writes: It favors commas followed by quote marks and disfavors sentence-ending periods after quotes, which says little about the label text.
card.plain: It fires on the first piece of a drug or enzyme name, or the small word right before one, in drug interaction and dosing text.
